title: Warm Ink — Broadsheet Chart Claim
description: A Financial Times–inspired chart-first layout where a single dominant column chart carries the argument, framed by a warm salmon card ground, sentence-form headline, and a rigorous 8pt italic source line. Different from peer dashboard templates in its refusal of multi-panel grids or decorative KPI tiles.
philosophy: This template holds that the chart is the claim — not an illustration of a bullet point someone already made. It imports the editorial discipline of the FT data desk: one chart, one full-sentence assertion above it, and one transparent source line below that earns the trust of a sceptical room. It rejects legend clutter, palette fireworks, and headline labels that merely name the data rather than argue from it. It is built for analysts, economists, and researchers who present to audiences that read numbers before they read prose.
goodFor: Quarterly earnings briefings anchored by a single decisive chart
Policy research presentations to expert or parliamentary audiences
Data journalism decks with annotated column or bar charts
Economics seminars where source provenance is openly scrutinised
avoidFor: Multi-KPI dashboard overviews that require six or more simultaneous panels
Brand identity or product marketing decks without quantitative argument
Team introduction or people-first narrative slides
Consumer-facing lifestyle, event, or promotional contexts
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the cover sheet of a confidential FT data desk briefing — warm, ink-on-parchment gravitas with a quiet editorial authority. Compositional rhythm is vertical and deliberately spare: one full-sentence claim centered in generous negative space, held in place by ruled lines rather than weight contrast or colour drama. Avoid any decorative motifs, gradient washes, or photographic texture. The mood is trustworthy restraint — the kind of opening that signals the argument will be won by evidence, not spectacle.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; deck title occupies cols 2–11 centered vertically in the upper two-thirds of the slide, with a thin horizontal rule above and below the headline block acting as the sole hierarchy device. Outer margin holds at roughly 8% on all sides — no edge bleed. A small-caps deck descriptor (series title or date) anchors bottom-right at baseline; no header band, no logo zone. The warm card ground fills the full slide field with no inset panel.

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a broadsheet data page from a serious financial daily — authoritative, spare, and quietly insistent. The chart dominates with editorial gravity, its mass doing the arguing so the headline above can speak in a full declarative sentence rather than a vague label. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric in vertical weight: dense chart body below, minimal prose assertion above, gossamer source line anchoring the foot. Avoid rounded-corner card stacking, palette variety beyond purposeful data encoding, and any decorative element that signals 'dashboard' over 'argument'.

examples.layoutNotes: Single 12-column grid; the chart occupies the full horizontal span across cols 1–12 and claims roughly 62% of vertical real estate, edge-padded by a consistent 6% outer margin on each side. A full-sentence headline sits in a tight single-row band immediately above the chart body, left-aligned, separated from it by a thin horizontal rule. Below the chart, a second rule line divides the chart floor from a flush-left italic source attribution at the slide baseline. No sidebar panels, no KPI tile strip, no floating legend box — any data labels live as inline bar annotations only.
